title: Rademacher sums exceed √2 standard deviations with probability at most 1/8
credit: Hollom and Portier, Conjecture 6.2 in arXiv:2306.07811 (2023); background Keller–Klein, Pinelis.
premise_risks: Edelman's unrefereed 2025 preprint arXiv:2508.13226 claims a general equal-weight theorem for mid-tails which would imply the claim; its correctness is doubtful (earlier version retracted after Pinelis's counterexample) but a scorer should know of it
Hollom–Portier preprint: publication venue not verified
plain: Take real weights a_1,...,a_n with a_1²+...+a_n²=1 and independent fair ±1 signs, and form X = Σ a_i ε_i. With three equal weights 1/√3, X equals √3 with probability 1/8, so P(X > √2) can be 1/8. Prove that P(X > √2) <= 1/8 for every n and all such weights.
math: For $n\ge1$ and $a\in\mathbb R^n$ with $\sum_i a_i^2=1$, let $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n$ be i.i.d. uniform on $\{\pm1\}$. Prove $\Pr\big(\sum_i a_i\varepsilon_i>\sqrt2\big)\le 1/8$; equivalently $\#\{\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}^n:\langle a,\varepsilon\rangle>\sqrt2\}\le 2^{n-3}$. (Equality is attained, e.g. $a=(1,1,1)/\sqrt3$.)
